finding.claim: GET /users has no authentication or tenant check. The org to query comes straight from the request, so any caller can list id and name of users in any organization (IDOR / missing authz). Whether this is reachable depends on unseen upstream middleware that sets req.pg. None is present in this file, and nothing binds org to a caller identity.
finding.sink: req.pg.query SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1 and res.json(rows)

trace.note: Route registered with no auth middleware or guard
Attacker-supplied org is used as the tenant filter with no comparison to a caller's org
Rows are returned to the requester

finding.guards_checked: The query is parameterized ($1), so there is no SQL injection. No app.use or auth middleware exists in the file, and the only file in the directory is db.js. Upstream middleware outside this directory could not be checked. If it does not enforce auth, any caller can enumerate users across all orgs.

verdict.guard_found: none (only parameterization at db.js:9, which prevents SQLi but not authz; no auth middleware in the file; req.pg is set by no code in this app, so it is not an auth control)
verdict.reason: db.js:8-10 registers GET /users with no auth middleware (the app has no app.use at all, and req.pg is never assigned in this file), and passes the caller-controlled req.query.org to the WHERE org filter at db.js:9 and returns the rows at db.js:10, so any anonymous caller can list users of any org.
